title: The Cone Line
hook: Cones and a crew. Your leftover highway number.
scene: Overcast morning on the Ribbon. You have not left the freeway. Orange cones stand along the right fog line; two workers in yellow wait past them. The left still looks like a clean number. The gantry overhead is blank. If you carry highway leftover through people on the deck, the cones will not catch you. The next paint is a shift, not a ramp.
decision: The work zone is already in the road. What do you do with speed and the lane?

options.text: Hold highway speed — the left is still open and the cones are only on the right
options.result: You keep the leftover. The workers do not move. A cone line is not a suggestion. You write a highway number through a place that already asked for less.

options.text: Cut right through the cone line to get past the crew first
options.result: You take the work as a pass. Orange goes under the plow. One of the yellow coats has to step. The shift was a lane change you were supposed to wait for, not invent.

options.text: Bleed speed now and follow the cones when they take the lane
options.result: You dump the leftover before the crew. When the cones step in, you take the lane they leave you. The workers stay workers. The Beetle stays a car in a zone, not a problem in one.

options.text: Stop in the travel lane until the workers wave you through
options.result: You plant a Beetle in a live work lane. The car behind you still has leftover. The crew did not ask for a fourth cone made of steel.

debrief: In a marked work zone, slow down and follow the lane the cones give you. Do not hold leftover highway speed past the crew. You lost the leftover before the shift.

source.psdp_skill: Skill eleven: highway driving – part one
source.teaching_target: Work zone: reduce speed, follow the taper and lane shift, do not hold highway leftover or cut the cone line.
